chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan, from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, the servant stands up and performs the voluntary prayer, and the Lord is amazed by His angels because of him, so He says: 'My angels, My servant performs what I did not make obligatory upon him.' As for the manner of performing it, he performs it according to what was missed by him, and that which indicates this.'

key_terms.يُعَجِّبُ: He makes amazing / He is amazed

ai.seo_question: How does one perform voluntary prayers to compensate for missed obligatory prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual elevation of voluntary prayers (nafl) as a means of perfecting obligatory duties, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding *kaffarat al-fawt* (compensation for missed acts). The divine amazement of the angels underscores the merit of going beyond the minimum requirements, reflecting the Quranic principle of striving for excellence (*ihsan*). This narration provides the textual basis for the scholarly view that nafl prayers can rectify minor defects or omissions in the fard prayers.
